title: The Discovery of Base Form
subtitle: Casting without a Rune, and why spellbooks look like star tables
summary: Base Form, discovered only after the first Forms, lets a person manifest a magical Word without a Rune, through a difficult mental calculation and a precise sound. It was the second revolution of the Era of Magic, and the reason a caster's most important possession is a book.
content:
> *"The first revolution taught us to use the Words. The second taught us to say them."*
> — a common way of putting it in the laboratories

At first, every Form depended on a Word from somewhere else. A caster could know Effect Glowing perfectly and still do nothing at all without a `Glow` Rune at hand, and Runes came only from the Gates, went dark after use, and could not be made (see [[runes-of-the-gates|Runes]]).

**Base Form** changed that. It is a method by which a person manifests a Word **themselves**, without a Rune to supply it. Its discovery was the second great revolution of the [[the-era-of-magic|Era of Magic]]: the first had shown that Gate magic could be manipulated by human technique; this one freed at least part of spellcasting from dependence on recovered artifacts.

## Second, Not First

The history of magic runs in what looks like the wrong order. The first Forms ([[the-first-three-forms|Effect Glowing, Simple Sauna and Kinetic Shove]]) came first. The Vocabulary of Words was isolated afterwards ([[the-vocabulary-breakthrough|The Vocabulary Breakthrough]]). Base Form came last of all. People learned to use Words before they learned to make them.

That is why it is called **Base** Form and never *Basic* Form. *Basic* suggests beginner's magic, the first thing a student learns. *Base* means foundation: the fundamental operation from which Forms draw their Words. It is not the easiest technique a caster learns, and for many it is the hardest.

Who first demonstrated Base Form, and when, is not recorded in this entry.

## One Word at a Time

There is no single Base Form. Each one manifests **one specific Word**, and each has to be learned separately: Base Form: Glow, Base Form: Heat, Base Form: Move, and so on. Understanding the theory of a Word does not let anyone manifest it, and nor does knowing a Form that uses it.

The result is highly specialised magical education. One caster may manifest `Move` and nothing else; another `Glow` and `Heat`; a third may know a dozen Forms and no Base Form at all, and rely entirely on Runes and Resources.

## A Calculation in the Head

Base Form does not look like a wizard reciting a spell. It looks like someone doing very difficult mathematics without paper.

To manifest a Word, the caster works through a complex derivation in their head, adjusted for the real world around them. The parameters can include the positions of celestial bodies, angles, distances, orientation, the time and local conditions. The caster works out the right values for this moment and this place and arrives at the solution. **The reasoning is part of what makes the magic happen.** Then the caster makes the required **sound**, a spoken syllable, a chant or a precise vocalisation, and the Word manifests.

Teachers like to show beginners an example equation of the kind a Base Form involves. Nobody pretends it is the real thing; it only shows the flavour:

> *1 + Sun Degrees above the Horizon / Local Temperature = X*

Why the universe should answer a correct derivation is not known. That it does, reliably, is the foundation of modern casting.

> **A student's letter home from Endros (excerpt)**
>
> *You asked what it is like. It is like the examination hall, except the examiner is the world, and you are sitting in it. You check the hour, you check where things are in the sky, you take the angle off the instrument, you carry the figures through, and halfway through you realise you used last week's table. So you start again. And when you finally have it, and you say the syllable, and the air answers, I promise you it is the best feeling there is. Then it fades, and you have to do it all again. Please send more pencils.*

## The Spellbook

Base Form is why casters carry books. A spellbook is genuine technical reference, without which the derivation cannot be done. It looks less like a book of incantations than a cross between:

- an advanced mathematics textbook;
- an astronomy handbook;
- a laboratory notebook and experimental manual;
- a pronunciation guide;
- tables of constants, charts and diagrams;
- years of corrections in the margins.

A single spell's pages might hold its governing equation at the top, a chart showing the positions of particular stars, lookup tables, a tool for turning observed conditions into the values the equation needs, known shortcuts, notes on derivations that failed, pronunciation marks, and worked examples of cases already solved. Every caster's book is different, and most are full of someone else's handwriting as well as their own.

> **Overheard at the University's receiving room in Endros**
>
> "I lost my book in the Gate."
>
> The clerk did not look up. "Which one?"
>
> "My *spellbook*."
>
> Now the clerk looked up, and her face changed. "Oh," she said, quite gently. "Sit down. I'll fetch someone. Did you have a copy?"

## What a Manifested Word Is Like

A Word manifested through Base Form does not last. It holds only so much, and every Form that draws on it uses some of that up. When it is exhausted, or simply when enough time has passed, it fades, and the caster must work the derivation again. How much a manifestation holds depends on how well the derivation went: a clean one gives a caster plenty to work with, a shaky one very little.

## Still Hard Work

Everything about Base Form today is inconvenient. A caster must have learned the method for each Word separately, must have their book and references to hand, must be able to carry the derivation through without error, and must be able to make the sound. Lose the book, or the voice, and the Word stays out of reach. That is simply where the science stands at the start of the Era of Magic.

It will not necessarily stay that way. Simpler equations, better notation, standard tables, memory techniques, instruments to help with the calculation, substitutes for the sound: every one of them is a plausible discovery, and none of them has been made yet. When they are, it will be because someone in Endros made them.
